key_insight: Leveraging generative modeling in pixel space yields "pixel-perfect" monocular depth that removes flying pixels and preserves fine geometric detail, enabling high-quality, artifact-free point clouds from single images.
problem_solved: Existing geometry foundation models produce noisy point clouds with flying pixels and lose fine surface details, limiting reliability for robotics, AR, and other 3D-aware applications.
method: Introduce Pixel-Perfect Depth (PPD), a monocular depth foundation model trained with generative/pixel-space objectives to directly model high-fidelity depth at the pixel level.
Design losses and architecture components that suppress flying pixels and recover fine-scale geometry, producing cleaner depth maps.
Convert high-quality depth predictions into point clouds with fewer artifacts for downstream 3D tasks.
impact: Provides practitioners with a more reliable, fine-detail-preserving depth foundation for robotics, AR, and 3D reconstruction, improving mapping, interaction, and visual localization performance.
visual_elements: Before/after depth-map comparison (standard model vs. PPD) highlighting removed flying pixels and restored edges
Point-cloud overlays from the same input image showing artifact reduction and finer surface detail
Pipeline diagram: input image → pixel-space generative depth model → clean depth map → point-cloud conversion
Quantitative bar/heatmap chart of error metrics (e.g., flying-pixel rate, depth RMSE, edge preservation) across baselines
paper_authors: Gangwei Xu, Haotong Lin, Hongcheng Luo, Haiyang Sun, Bing Wang
